hook.line: Watch this: go here and click download.
hook.visual: Man in a cap at his desk; app-icon equation 'Codex + Claude = fire' on top and a 'together is an unfair cheat code' label; at 1.12 s a pencil points at the screen.

beats.what: Icon equation (Codex icon + Claude icon = fire emoji) and bold claim label over a desk shot.
Hard cut to filmed monitor; a pencil taps the download button as he says 'go here'.
Quick cuts through the install steps: open app, toggle terminal.
Close-up of the terminal: type Claude, hit enter, with zoom punches on each step.
Cut to selfie close-up: the reframe, it can be Claude Code and Codex.
Division of labour: Claude designs, Codex builds; cheaper on two $20 plans.
Cutaway to his written guide with blue label 'Drop GUIDE and I'll send you the link'.
Back to face: 'the two best models working together feels unfair', then follow ask.

why_it_works: Demo before explanation: the install is shown in the first 10 s, so the 'why' lands after the viewer has already seen it work.
The app-icon equation reads instantly without words and makes the topic clear in frame one.
Fast cuts (11.67 per min) and zoom punches during the steps match a quick speaking rate (4.19 words/s).
Comment keyword 'GUIDE' turns the CTA into an engagement trigger and shows the guide as proof it exists.
weaknesses: Filmed-monitor shots with a pencil pointer are blurry; the exact clicks are hard to follow.
Two CTAs (comment GUIDE, then follow) compete in the last 6 s.
for_robert: Open with a tiny visual equation (icon + icon = result) above his head; Fred could slap the pieces into place one by one as he says them.
